# old-school: email on a single shared machine

### scenario:

*  multiple users logging into shared machine
*  "mail" service for them...

### sending `mail` locally?

<pre><code>
testuser@ourserver:~$ <b>mail charles</b>
Cc: 
Subject: <b>another demo email</b>

<b>This is another demo email.</b>
<b><i>&lt;control-D&gt;</i></b>
testuser@ourserver:~$ 
</code></pre>

### simple local mail implementation

*  mail "spool" file with appropriate permissions for each user
*  mail sending program marked set-group-ID
   *  modify other user's spool files
*  locking scheme to avoid concurrent modification

### terminology

*  SMTP (Simple Mail Transport Protocol)
   *  the standard for sending internet email
*  Mail User Agent (MUA)
   *  a program used to send/receive emails
   *  what humans actually interact with
*  Mail Transfer Agent (MTA)
   *  a program that transfers mail to another program
   *  MUAs are a special case

### things we'll need for "real" email

*  find out right machine to get email to
   *  issue: domain name in address != right machine
*  handling errors
   *  retry sending later
   *  telling user if sending later failed
   *  issue: needs to be done by program running after mail "sent"
*  sending to multiple people
*  reading emails not from a local file

### address format {.smaller}

*  RFC 5322
<hr/>
*  `Name For Humans <username@dns.name.example>`
*  `username@dns.name.example`
   *  this part called "addr-spec"
*  destination is from _MX record_ for dns.name.example
<hr/>
*  `username@[machine.dns.name.example]`
*  `username@[203.0.113.5]`
*  destination is machine.dns.name.exmaple/203.0.113.5

### MX records {.smaller}

```
gmail.com.              639     IN      MX      5 gmail-smtp-in.l.google.com.
gmail.com.              639     IN      MX      10 alt1.gmail-smtp-in.l.google.com.
gmail.com.              639     IN      MX      20 alt2.gmail-smtp-in.l.google.com.
gmail.com.              639     IN      MX      30 alt3.gmail-smtp-in.l.google.com.
gmail.com.              639     IN      MX      40 alt4.gmail-smtp-in.l.google.com.
```
<hr/>
*  5/10/20/... is preference (lower = more preferred) 
*  client should try servers in order
   *  lookup A or AAAA record for each
   *  use first that works
*  if no MX record, fallback to looking up address for name

### layers of forwarding

*  emails to <i>xyz</i>@virginia.edu would go to mailbox on...
   *  Microsoft-hosted email servers
   *  Google-hosted email servers (during transition)
   *  ticketing systems (cshelpdesk@virginia.edu, ...)
   *  mailing list systems (csugrads@virginia.edu, ...)
   *  ...
*  likely all hosted on different servers
*  MX record will only have one of those...

### email relays

*  many mail servers are relays
   *  collect message, send on to actual destination
*  "submission servers" --- special case of relays
   *  mail user agent sends message to one submission server, then forgets about it
   *  simplifies logic of mail user agents
   *  submission server can handle retrying, etc.

*  _find out right machine to get email to_
   *  issue: domain name in address != right machine

### SMTP protocol basics

*  text-based, stateful protocol
   *  stateful = not series of independent operations like HTTP
*  build up "mail transactions" (sending one message)
*  client sends sequence of commands:
   *  4-character command name followed by arguments
*  server replies with status code + message
   *  similar 3-digit status codes to HTTP

### example SMTP session {.smaller}

*  S=server, C=client

```
S: 220 foo.com Simple Mail Transfer Service Ready
C: EHLO bar.com
S: 250-foo.com greets bar.com
S: 250-8BITMIME
S: 250-SIZE
S: 250-DSN
S: 250 HELP
C: MAIL FROM:<Smith@bar.com>
S: 250 OK
C: RCPT TO:<Jones@foo.com>
S: 250 OK
C: RCPT TO:<Green@foo.com>
S: 550 No such user here
C: RCPT TO:<Brown@foo.com>
S: 250 OK
C: DATA
S: 354 Start mail input; end with <CRLF>.<CRLF>
C: Blah blah blah...
C: ...etc. etc. etc.
C: .
S: 250 OK
C: QUIT
```

### general command format {.smaller}

*  $\text{client}\rightarrow\text{server}$: `XCMD arg1 arg2 arg3`
   *  `XCMD` is 4 character command name
   *  arguments are space-separated
   *  terminated by CRLF
*  $\text{server}\rightarrow\text{client}$: `999-line1`<br/>
   $\text{server}\rightarrow\text{client}$: `999-line2`<br/>
   $\text{server}\rightarrow\text{client}$: `999 line3`<br/>
   *  three-line reply, each line terminated with CRLF
   *  starts with three-digit status code
   *  `-` = not complete reply

### status codes

*  details: RFC 5321, sec 4.2
*  2xx = okay, complete
*  3xx = okay, still more to do
*  4xx = error, you should retry
*  5xx = error, you should not retry

### connection setup

*  `EHLO` (extended hello)
    *  also deprecated HELO
*  server replies with greeting line, list of non-required commands it implements

```
C: EHLO bar.com
S: 250-foo.com greets bar.com
S: 250-8BITMIME
S: 250-SIZE
S: 250-DSN
S: 250 HELP
```

### mail transactions

*  steps:
   *  set sender ("reverse path")
   *  set recepients
   *  send data
